Basics of Income Tax.front: Which year is the 'Previous Year' and which is the 'Assessment Year' — name the sections.
Basics of Income Tax.back: Previous Year = year immediately preceding the Assessment Year (sec 3); Assessment Year = year immediately following the Previous Year (sec 2(9)).

Basics of Income Tax.front: Which section creates the charge of income‑tax on a person for an assessment year?
Basics of Income Tax.back: Section 4: Charge of income‑tax — income of every person is chargeable to income‑tax for the assessment year.

Basics of Income Tax.front: Which incomes are taxable in India irrespective of the taxpayer's residence (which section)?
Basics of Income Tax.back: Sec 5: Income accruing or arising in India, or deemed to accrue/arise in India, is taxable in India regardless of the person's residence.

Basics of Income Tax.front: Name the five heads of income that must be computed separately (section).
Basics of Income Tax.back: 5 heads: Salaries; House‑Property; Profits & Gains of Business/Profession; Capital Gains; Other Sources (sec 14).

Basics of Income Tax.front: Who is a 'person' under the Income‑tax Act — give the statutory reference.
Basics of Income Tax.back: Sec 2(31): Person includes individual, HUF, company, firm, AOP/BOI, local authority and any other juridical/artificial person.

Basics of Income Tax.front: Give the numeric tests under s.6(1) when an individual becomes 'resident'.
Basics of Income Tax.back: 182 days OR 60 days + 365 days: Individual is resident if in India ≥182 days in PY, or ≥60 days in PY and ≥365 days in the 4 preceding years (s.6(1)).

Basics of Income Tax.front: What numeric tests determine 'ordinarily resident' under s.6(6)?
Basics of Income Tax.back: 2 & 730: OR requires resident in at least 2 of the 10 preceding years AND stayed ≥730 days in India during the 7 preceding years (s.6(6)); otherwise RNOR.

Basics of Income Tax.front: When does s.6(1A) deem an Indian citizen to be resident?
Basics of Income Tax.back: Indian CITIZEN (not PIO) + total income other than from foreign sources above ₹15 lakh + not liable to tax in any other country by reason of domicile or residence. Always RNOR (s.6(6)(d)).

Basics of Income Tax.front: State the concise sequence (main steps) to compute tax from receipts to tax payable.
Basics of Income Tax.back: 5 steps: Compute income under 5 heads → Aggregate Gross Total Income → Deduct Chapter VI‑A → Arrive at Total Income → Compute tax, apply rebates/relief (then cess/interest).

Basics of Income Tax.front: What is the classic difference between Sec 5 and Sec 9 of the Act?
Basics of Income Tax.back: Sec5 = charging provision that defines taxable scope; Sec9 = lists specific events/sources deemed to accrue/arise in India (e.g., business connection, transfer of India‑situated assets).

Income from House Property.front: Give the exact computation sequence from Annual Value to Income from House Property (name sections).
Income from House Property.back: 5 steps: 1) Annual Value (s.23); 2) Less municipal taxes paid by owner; 3) Net Annual Value; 4) Less 30% standard deduction (s.24(a)) and interest on borrowed capital (s.24(b)); 5) Income from House Property (s.22).

Income from House Property.front: State the standard deduction from Net Annual Value and its legal provision.
Income from House Property.back: 30% of Net Annual Value as standard deduction under section 24(a).

Income from House Property.front: Interest on borrowed capital u/s 24(b): let-out vs self-occupied, old vs new regime?
Income from House Property.back: Let-out: full interest, no ceiling. Self-occupied (old regime): ₹2,00,000, or ₹30,000 if conditions fail. New regime: NIL for self-occupied. Pre-construction interest: 5 equal instalments from year of completion.

Income from House Property.front: When are municipal taxes deductible and how do they affect Gross Annual Value?
Income from House Property.back: Municipal taxes actually paid by the owner in the year are deductible from Gross Annual Value (reduce GAV) (s.23(1)).

Income from House Property.front: How do you arrive at Gross Annual Value of a let-out house?
Income from House Property.back: Step 1: expected rent = higher of municipal value and fair rent, capped at standard rent. Step 2: GAV = higher of expected rent and actual rent received or receivable (s.23(1)). Vacancy can pull GAV below expected rent.

Income from House Property.front: How many houses can be treated as self-occupied with nil annual value?
Income from House Property.back: TWO, at the owner's option (s.23(2)/(4)). A third and further houses are deemed let out and taxed on expected rent. The ₹2,00,000 interest ceiling covers both self-occupied houses together.

Income from House Property.front: Co-owned house with definite shares: how is it taxed, and what does each co-owner get?
Income from House Property.back: Each co-owner is assessed separately on his share (s.26). For a self-occupied house, EACH co-owner gets the full ₹2,00,000 interest limit (old regime) — it is not split.

Income from House Property.front: When is rent included in Gross Annual Value — what does 'received or receivable' mean?
Income from House Property.back: Rent is taxable on a 'received or receivable' basis — included in GAV when due (receivable) or actually received during the year (s.23).

Income from House Property.front: Are actual repairs, insurance and collection charges separately deductible in addition to the standard deduction?
Income from House Property.back: No. 30% standard deduction on NAV (s.24(a)) is a composite allowance for repairs, insurance and collection charges; no separate deduction for these items thereafter.

Income from House Property.front: How are arrears of rent / unrealised rent recovered later taxed?
Income from House Property.back: s.25A: taxed in the year of RECEIPT under house property, after a flat 30% deduction — even if the assessee no longer owns the property.

Income from House Property.front: Can a house property loss be set off against salary: old regime vs new regime?
Income from House Property.back: Old regime: yes, up to ₹2,00,000 a year (s.71(3A)); balance carried forward 8 years against HP income only. New regime: NO set-off against any other head.

Income from House Property.front: When are municipal taxes deductible from GAV?
Income from House Property.back: Only when actually PAID by the OWNER during the year — even if they relate to earlier years. Not if merely due, and not if borne by the tenant.

Residential Status.front: State the 182‑day rule for an individual’s residence (exact days and section).
Residential Status.back: 182 days: Individual is resident if present in India for 182 days or more in the previous year (section 6(1)).

Residential Status.front: State the alternative short‑stay condition that also makes an individual resident (exact days and preceding‑years test).
Residential Status.back: 60 days + 365 days: Individual resident if present in India for 60 days or more in the previous year AND for 365 days or more during the 4 preceding years (section 6(1)).

Residential Status.front: s.6(1A) deemed residency — the three conditions?
Residential Status.back: (1) Indian CITIZEN only, not PIO; (2) total income other than foreign-source income exceeds ₹15 lakh; (3) not liable to tax in any other country. Result: deemed resident, and always RNOR.

Residential Status.front: When is a resident individual 'not ordinarily resident' (RNOR)?
Residential Status.back: If EITHER: non-resident in 9 out of 10 preceding years, OR in India for 729 days or less in the 7 preceding years (s.6(6)). Fail both escape routes = ROR.

Residential Status.front: Define 'Resident but not Ordinarily Resident' (RNOR) and state precisely which foreign income is taxable.
Residential Status.back: RNOR: resident who fails ROR tests (s.6). Taxable: income received/ deemed received in India; income accruing/ arising/ deemed to arise in India; foreign income only if from business controlled or profession set up in India.

Residential Status.front: What income is taxable in India for a Non‑Resident (NR)? Give the exact categories.
Residential Status.back: 2 categories: income received or deemed to be received in India; income accruing or arising or deemed to arise in India (i.e., India‑sourced income).

Residential Status.front: How should you count days of stay in India for residence tests?
Residential Status.back: Count days: calendar days; any part‑day in India counts as a day; day of arrival and day of departure are included when determining total days of stay.

Residential Status.front: When is a company resident in India? And a firm / HUF / AOP?
Residential Status.back: Company: Indian company, OR its place of effective management (POEM) is in India in that year (s.6(3)). Firm/HUF/AOP: resident unless control and management is WHOLLY outside India.

Residential Status.front: Give the stepwise procedure (the one students often skip) to determine an individual’s final residential status.
Residential Status.back: 2 steps: (1) Apply residence tests (182 days OR 60+365) to decide Resident/NR (s.6(1)). (2) If Resident, apply ROR tests (2/10 years and 730/7 years) to classify ROR or RNOR — many forget step 2.

Residential Status.front: State precisely the tax incidence for an Ordinary Resident (ROR).
Residential Status.back: Worldwide: ROR is taxed on global income (income received/earned/declared anywhere) — scope of total income under section 5 (resident ordinarily taxed on worldwide income).

Residential Status.front: Indian citizen LEAVES India for employment or as ship's crew — which residence test applies?
Residential Status.back: Only the 182-day test. The 60-day condition is replaced by 182 days (Explanation 1(a) to s.6(1)), so the 60 + 365 route is unavailable.

Residential Status.front: Indian citizen or PIO VISITING India — when does 60 days become 120 days?
Residential Status.back: If income other than foreign-source income exceeds ₹15 lakh: 120 days + 365 days in 4 preceding years makes him resident (and RNOR). If such income is ₹15 lakh or less: only the 182-day test applies.

Income from Salary.front: State the standard deduction available against salary and cite the section; old vs new regime amounts for AY 2026-27.
What three amounts are compared for HRA exemption and the metro/non‑metro percentages?
Income from Salary.back: Least of: actual HRA received; rent paid minus 10% of salary; 50% (metro) / 40% (non‑metro) of salary. Rule/section: Sec 10(13A) (HRA rules).

Income from Salary.front: What are the exact conditions and limits for LTA exemption?
Income from Salary.back: Two journeys in a block of 4 years; travel only within India; exemption limited to actual travel fare. Exemption under Section 10(5).

Income from Salary.front: What is the entertainment allowance deduction for government employees (limits and rule)?
Income from Salary.back: Least of: actual entertainment allowance; 20% of salary; ₹5,000. Deduction under section 16(ii) (available to government employees only).

Income from Salary.front: State the exemption limits for children's education allowance and hostel allowance (per child, max children).
Income from Salary.back: Children's education allowance: ₹100 per month per child (max 2 children). Hostel allowance: ₹300 per month per child (max 2 children). (Allowances under Rule/section for exempt allowances.)

Income from Salary.front: What deduction is allowed for professional tax when computing taxable salary?
Income from Salary.back: Amount of professional tax actually paid is deductible under section 16(iii). No separate monetary cap beyond actual tax paid.

Income from Salary.front: Order of steps to compute taxable salary?
Income from Salary.back: Gross salary (basic + allowances + perquisites + profits in lieu) → less exempt allowances and exempt retirement benefits → less s.16 deductions (standard deduction; old regime also entertainment allowance and professional tax).

Income from Salary.front: What is the gratuity exemption limit and the position for government employees?
Income from Salary.back: ₹20,00,000 maximum exemption under section 10(10) (statutory gratuity). For government employees, gratuity received is fully exempt (subject to provisions).

Income from Salary.front: How are 'profits in lieu of salary' treated and where are they charged?
Income from Salary.back: Profits in lieu of salary (compensation on termination, retrenchment etc.) taxable under section 17(3) except amounts exempt under sec 10(10)/10(10A)/10(10B as applicable).

Income from Salary.front: What is the 'specified employee' salary threshold used in valuation rules (Rule 3C)?
Income from Salary.back: ₹4,00,000 salary threshold for 'specified employee' under Rule 3C (affects certain perquisite valuation rules).

Income from Salary.front: What gross total income limit applies for employer‑paid medical treatment abroad per Rule 3D?
Income from Salary.back: Gross total income ceiling ₹8,00,000 under Rule 3D for valuation/exemption considerations regarding employer‑paid medical travel abroad.

Income from Salary.front: Where are perquisites defined and valued?
Income from Salary.back: Defined in s.17(2); valued under Rule 3 of the Income-tax Rules. Rule 3C and 3D carry the new ₹4,00,000 and ₹8,00,000 limits.

Income from Salary.front: Rent-free unfurnished accommodation owned by a private employer — perquisite value?
Income from Salary.back: 10% of salary if population above 40 lakh; 7.5% if above 15 lakh up to 40 lakh; 5% otherwise (2011 census; Rule 3 from 1-9-2023). The old 15% / 10% / 7.5% rates are superseded.

Income from Salary.front: Leave encashment at retirement — exemption ceiling for non-government employees?
Income from Salary.back: ₹25,00,000 (s.10(10AA)); least of the ceiling, actual amount, 10 months' average salary, and unavailed leave at max 30 days a year. Encashment DURING service is fully taxable.

Income from Salary.front: Employer's contributions to PF + NPS + superannuation — when taxable?
Income from Salary.back: The aggregate above ₹7,50,000 in a year is a perquisite (s.17(2)(vii)), and so is the annual accretion on that excess. Separately, employer's PF contribution above 12% of salary is taxable.

Income from Salary.front: Commuted pension — how much is exempt for a non-government employee?
Income from Salary.back: 1/3 of the FULL commuted value if he also gets gratuity; 1/2 if he does not (s.10(10A)). Gross up first: full value = amount received ÷ percentage commuted. Government employees: fully exempt.

Income from Salary.front: Which salary deductions/exemptions die in the new regime?
Income from Salary.back: HRA, LTA, children education and hostel allowance, professional tax, entertainment allowance. What survives: standard deduction ₹75,000 and employer's NPS contribution u/s 80CCD(2).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: Which section governs intra‑head set‑off of loss from one source against income from another source in the same head?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. Section 70: Loss from one source under the same head may be set off against income from another source under that head in the same AY (intra‑head set‑off).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: What is the prescribed sequence to adjust losses when computing total income?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. Order: intra‑head set‑off (s.70) → inter‑head set‑off in same AY (s.71) → compute total income → carry forward unadjusted losses under relevant sections.

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: How long can a non‑speculative business loss be carried forward and against which income can it be set off?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. 8 assessment years; set off only against profits & gains of business or profession (carry‑forward rules: s.72).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: What are the set‑off and carry‑forward rules for speculative business losses?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. Set off in same AY only against speculative gains; unabsorbed speculative loss carried forward 4 assessment years and can be set off only against speculative gains (s.73).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: How are short‑term and long‑term capital losses adjusted and what is the carry‑forward period?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. STCL: set off against STCG and LTCG; LTCL: set off only against LTCG. 2. Carry forward for 8 assessment years (s.74).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: House property loss — set-off and carry forward?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: Old regime: set off against other heads up to ₹2,00,000 a year (s.71(3A)); balance carried forward 8 AYs against house property income only (s.71B). New regime: no inter-head set-off.

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: What is the rule for unabsorbed depreciation (carry forward and set‑off)?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. Unabsorbed depreciation: carried forward without limit and set off in subsequent years until exhausted; can be adjusted against any head's income (as per s.32 read with carry‑forward provisions).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: Which losses are restricted to be set off only against income of the same head (give examples and periods)?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. LTC loss → only LTCG; Speculation loss → only speculative gains (4 years); Business loss (carried forward) → only business income (8 years); House property carried forward → only house property (8 years).

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: Which losses need a return filed by the s.139(1) due date to be carried forward?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: Business loss (incl. speculation and specified business), capital loss, and loss from owning race horses (s.80). EXCEPTIONS: house property loss and unabsorbed depreciation carry forward even with a belated return.

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: What is the single common computational step students often miss when setting off losses?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: 1. Always perform intra‑head adjustments first (s.70) before inter‑head set‑off; failure to do intra‑head set‑off first leads to incorrect remaining loss and wrong carry‑forward amount.

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: Can business loss be set off against salary income?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: No — s.71(2A) bars set-off of loss under PGBP against income under 'Salaries'. It can be set off against the other heads.

Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.front: Specified business loss (s.35AD) and loss from owning race horses — rules?
Set off and Carry Forward of Losses.back: s.73A: specified business loss only against specified business income, carried forward indefinitely. s.74A: race-horse loss only against race-horse income, carried forward 4 AYs. Losses from lottery/betting cannot be set off at all.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.44AD — turnover limit, rates, and the 5-year rule?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Up to ₹2 crore; ₹3 crore if cash receipts do not exceed 5% of turnover. Income = 8% of turnover, 6% on receipts through banking channels. Declare lower and opt out → barred from 44AD for the next 5 AYs.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.44ADA — limit and deemed income for professionals?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Gross receipts up to ₹50 lakh; ₹75 lakh if cash receipts do not exceed 5%. Income = 50% of gross receipts. Unlike 44AD there is no 5-year lock-out.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: Give the tax‑audit turnover limits for businesses and professionals under section 44AB, and the higher‑limit condition.
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: 1 crore turnover for business (raised to 10 crore if cash receipts/payments ≤5% of total); 50 lakh gross receipts for professionals. (s.44AB).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: What is the cash payment limit under s.40A(3) and what happens if it is breached?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: 10,000; if payment in cash exceeds ₹10,000 the entire payment is disallowed as a business expense (not just the excess). (s.40A(3)).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: When are deductions under s.43B allowable? Give the payment deadline condition and examples.
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Due date of filing return u/s139(1); deductions under s.43B allowed only if actually paid on or before that date. Examples: tax, employer's PF, gratuity, bonus, leave encashment. (s.43B).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: How is depreciation computed for tax under s.32 — basis and block treatment?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: WDV; depreciation computed on block of assets at rates in Income‑tax Rules; add cost of additions, subtract disposals, then apply prescribed rate. (s.32).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: Under what precise condition is an expenditure allowable under s.37(1)?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Wholly and exclusively for business; not capital, not personal, and not covered by specific sections s.30–s.36. (s.37(1)).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.40(a)(ia) vs s.40(a)(i) — how much is disallowed for TDS default?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Payment to a RESIDENT: 30% of the sum disallowed. Payment to a NON-RESIDENT: 100%. Either is allowed in the year the tax is deducted and paid.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: Write the stepwise order to compute taxable profits from profit & gains of business/profession.
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: 1) Start with P&L net profit; 2) add back non‑allowable items (s40/40A); 3) add business incomes taxed elsewhere; 4) deduct allowable expenses (s30–s37) and depreciation (s32).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.40(b) — maximum remuneration to working partners?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: On first ₹6,00,000 of book profit (or loss): ₹3,00,000 or 90% of book profit, whichever is higher. On the balance: 60%. Must be authorised by the deed. Interest to partners capped at 12% p.a.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: When is a bad debt deductible under s.36?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: If previously included in income and subsequently written off as irrecoverable — bad debt deductible under s.36(1)(vii). Banks have special provisions. (s.36(1)(vii)).

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.40A(3) — what is the limit for payments to a transporter?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: ₹35,000 per day for plying, hiring or leasing goods carriages (general limit ₹10,000). Cross the limit and the WHOLE payment is disallowed, not the excess.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.43B(h) — payments to micro and small enterprises?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Deductible only on ACTUAL PAYMENT if not paid within the MSMED Act limit (45 days with written agreement, 15 days without). Paying before the return due date does NOT save it.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: Employees' PF contribution deposited late — treatment?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: It is the employer's income u/s 2(24)(x); deduction u/s 36(1)(va) only if deposited by the due date under the PF law. The 'before return due date' relief of s.43B covers only the EMPLOYER'S own contribution.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: Depreciation when an asset is used for less than 180 days? Additional depreciation?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Under 180 days: half the normal rate. Additional depreciation: 20% on new plant and machinery for manufacturers (10% if under 180 days, balance next year) — NOT available in the new regime.

Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.front: s.44AE — presumptive income for goods carriages?
Profits and Gains from Business or Profe.back: Up to 10 vehicles. Heavy goods vehicle: ₹1,000 per tonne of gross vehicle weight per month or part. Other vehicles: ₹7,500 per month or part. A part of a month counts as a full month.

Capital Gains.front: s.112A — rate, exemption and the grandfathering cost rule?
Capital Gains.back: 12.5% on LTCG above ₹1,25,000 from STT-paid listed equity/equity funds, no indexation. Cost = higher of (a) actual cost and (b) LOWER of FMV on 31-1-2018 and sale price. It can wipe out a gain but never create a loss.

Capital Gains.front: How is short‑term capital gain on sale of listed equity/units (where STT paid) taxed and under which section?
Capital Gains.back: 20%: STCG on securities where STT paid is taxed at 20% under s.111A (sale on recognised stock exchange, STT requirement essential).

Capital Gains.front: LTCG on land or building sold by a resident individual/HUF — which rate?
Capital Gains.back: Acquired BEFORE 23-7-2024: tax = lower of 12.5% without indexation and 20% with indexation. Acquired on or after that date, and for all other assessees and assets: 12.5% without indexation.

Capital Gains.front: Holding‑period thresholds to treat as long‑term: (a) listed equity/units (b) other assets.
Capital Gains.back: 12 months / 24 months: Listed equity/units = long‑term if >12 months; other capital assets = long‑term if >24 months.

Capital Gains.front: s.54 — time limits, cap and the two-house option?
Capital Gains.back: Buy within 1 year before or 2 years after, or construct within 3 years. Cost of new house counted up to ₹10 crore. If LTCG is up to ₹2 crore, may invest in TWO houses — once in a lifetime.

Capital Gains.front: s.54F — how is the exemption computed and what is the ownership condition?
Capital Gains.back: Exemption = LTCG × amount invested ÷ NET CONSIDERATION. Must not own more than one residential house (other than the new one) on the date of transfer. ₹10 crore cap applies. Asset sold must NOT be a residential house.

Capital Gains.front: Give the limit, time‑window and lock‑in for investment under section 54EC.
Capital Gains.back: ₹50,00,000: invest in notified bonds within 6 months of transfer; bonds locked‑in for 5 years; applies to LTCG from land or building (s.54EC).

Capital Gains.front: What is the three‑step computation sequence for capital gain (name the section reference)?
Capital Gains.back: 1) Full value of consideration; 2) Less cost of transfer/expenses; 3) Less (indexed) cost of acquisition & improvement = capital gain (s.48; use CII where indexation allowed).

Capital Gains.front: How do set‑off and carry‑forward rules work between short‑term and long‑term capital losses?
Capital Gains.back: STCL can be set off against STCG or LTCG; LTCL only against LTCG; unabsorbed losses carried forward for 8 assessment years if return filed within due date.

Capital Gains.front: Whose cost is used when an asset is received as a gift for computing capital gains on later transfer?
Capital Gains.back: Cost of previous owner: recipient inherits previous owner's cost and acquisition date for capital gains computation (s.49 applies to such provisions).

Capital Gains.front: How do you compute indexed cost using the Cost Inflation Index (CII)?
Capital Gains.back: Indexed cost = Actual cost × (CII of year of transfer / CII of year of acquisition); apply where indexation benefit is available (used in s.48 computations).

Capital Gains.front: What base‑cost rule applies to assets acquired before 1‑4‑2001 for capital gains computation?
Capital Gains.back: FMV rule: for assets acquired before 01‑04‑2001, use higher of actual cost or FMV as on 01‑04‑2001 as base for computing capital gains (then apply indexation forward).

Capital Gains.front: s.50C — when does stamp duty value replace actual consideration?
Capital Gains.back: Only if stamp value exceeds 110% of the consideration. If it does, the WHOLE stamp value is adopted. Same 10% tolerance in s.43CA and s.56(2)(x).

Capital Gains.front: Sale of depreciable assets (s.50) — nature of the gain?
Capital Gains.back: ALWAYS short-term, whatever the holding period. Gain arises when sale value exceeds opening WDV + additions, or the block ceases to exist.

Capital Gains.front: Buyback of shares on or after 1-10-2024 — tax in the shareholder's hands?
Capital Gains.back: Entire amount received is DIVIDEND (s.2(22)(f)), no deduction for cost. For capital gains the consideration is nil, so the cost becomes a capital LOSS to set off or carry forward.

Capital Gains.front: Capital asset converted into stock-in-trade — when and on what value is gain taxed?
Capital Gains.back: s.45(2): capital gain taxed in the year the stock is SOLD, using FMV on the date of conversion as consideration. Sale price minus that FMV is business income.

Income from Other Sources.front: Which section is the charging provision for Income from Other Sources and what incomes does it residually include (one line)?
Income from Other Sources.back: 56: residuary head — incomes not chargeable under Salaries, HP, PGBP or CG (s.56); includes dividends, interest, family pension, gifts, winnings, other residual receipts.

Income from Other Sources.front: When are gifts/monetary receipts from non‑relatives taxable? Name the threshold and main exemptions.
Income from Other Sources.back: ₹50,000: gifts/monies from non‑relatives aggregating >₹50,000 taxable under s.56(2); gifts from relatives, on marriage, by will, local authorities, recognised institutions are exempt.

Income from Other Sources.front: Immovable property bought for inadequate consideration — when is the difference taxed?
Income from Other Sources.back: s.56(2)(x): only if stamp value exceeds consideration by more than the HIGHER of ₹50,000 and 10% of the consideration. If it does, the whole difference is taxable.

Income from Other Sources.front: How are shares, securities or movable property received for inadequate or no consideration taxed (give the numeric test)?
Income from Other Sources.back: ₹50,000: FMV minus consideration of movable property/shares/securities received without/for inadequate consideration is taxable if FMV>₹50,000 (s.56(2)); listed/unlisted securities have specific rules.

Income from Other Sources.front: What is the general rule for deductions against Income from Other Sources and which section governs it?
Income from Other Sources.back: 57: only expenses 'wholly and exclusively' for earning IFS are deductible — e.g. interest, manager/agent remuneration, collection/repairs, taxes; no general standard deduction (s.57).

Income from Other Sources.front: Family pension — deduction in old vs new regime?
Income from Other Sources.back: s.57(iia): lower of 1/3 of the pension and ₹15,000 (old regime) or ₹25,000 (new regime). Taxed under Other Sources, never Salaries.

Income from Other Sources.front: Lottery, races, card games, online games — how taxed?
Income from Other Sources.back: Flat 30% (s.115BB; online games s.115BBJ on net winnings). No basic exemption, no deduction of any expense, no set-off of losses; in the new regime no 87A rebate against it.

Income from Other Sources.front: Dividend income — what expense can be deducted?
Income from Other Sources.back: Only INTEREST expense, and only up to 20% of the dividend (proviso to s.57). Commission or any other expense: nil.

Income from Other Sources.front: What is the TDS threshold for interest relevant to Income from Other Sources (s.194A)?
Income from Other Sources.back: ₹50,000 (₹1,00,000 for senior citizens): TDS under s.194A on interest is required when interest income exceeds ₹50,000; senior‑citizen threshold is ₹1,00,000.

Income from Other Sources.front: Are dividends exempt or taxable in the shareholder's hands now — name the change and year?
Income from Other Sources.back: 2020: DDT abolished (Finance Act 2020); dividends are now taxable as 'Income from Other Sources' in the recipient's hands — s.10(34) exemption removed.

Income from Other Sources.front: Interest on compensation or enhanced compensation — when taxed and what deduction?
Income from Other Sources.back: Taxed in the year of RECEIPT (s.145B), with a flat 50% deduction (s.57(iv)). No other deduction.

Income from Other Sources.front: Gifts that are NOT taxable u/s 56(2)(x)?
Income from Other Sources.back: From relatives; on the individual's own marriage (from anyone); under a will or inheritance; in contemplation of death of the donor; from local authority or registered trust. Otherwise taxable in full once aggregate exceeds ₹50,000.

Deductions.front: Maximum deduction under Section 80C for AY 2026–27 — amount and does 80CCD(1) fall within it?
Deductions.back: ₹1,50,000 — Section 80C. Yes: employee contribution under Section 80CCD(1) counts within the ₹1.5 lakh aggregate limit.

Deductions.front: How much extra deduction is allowed under Section 80CCD(1B) and who can claim it?
Deductions.back: ₹50,000 additional — Section 80CCD(1B). Resident individual NPS subscribers (includes NPS Vatsalya account for minors) — over and above the ₹1.5 lakh 80C limit.

Deductions.front: s.80CCD(2) — employer's NPS contribution: limit, and does it survive the new regime?
Deductions.back: Yes, it survives. New regime: up to 14% of salary (basic + DA) for all employers. Old regime: 10% for non-government employers, 14% government. Over and above the ₹1.5 lakh limit of s.80CCE.

Deductions.front: Section 80D: limits for health insurance premium deduction (self/family and parents) and preventive check‑ups?
Deductions.back: Self & family: ₹25,000 (₹50,000 if taxpayer ≥60); Parents: ₹25,000 (₹50,000 if parents ≥60). Preventive health check‑up max ₹5,000 within these limits — Section 80D.

Deductions.front: How long and how much interest on education loan is deductible under Section 80E?
Deductions.back: Interest fully deductible for up to 8 years from the year repayment begins (or until interest extinguished); no monetary ceiling — Section 80E. Applies to loan for higher education for self, spouse or children.

Deductions.front: What are the basic 80G rules: deduction rates and the 10% qualifying limit?
Deductions.back: Donations qualify for 100% or 50% deduction (with or without restriction) — Section 80G. Where restricted, deductible amount limited to 10% of Gross Total Income (computed before 80G deductions).

Deductions.front: Section 80GG: formula for rent deduction and key eligibility conditions?
Deductions.back: Deduction = least of: ₹5,000/month; 25% of total income; rent paid minus 10% of total income — Section 80GG. For those not receiving HRA, not owning accommodation at workplace/residence; file Form 10BA.

Deductions.front: Which Chapter VI-A deductions are available in the NEW regime?
Deductions.back: Only 80CCD(2) (employer's NPS), 80CCH(2) (Agniveer corpus) and 80JJAA. Everything else — 80C, 80D, 80E, 80G, 80TTA/TTB — is switched off.

Deductions.front: Interest on savings bank deposits — limits under Sections 80TTA and 80TTB?
Deductions.back: Non‑senior individuals/HUF: up to ₹10,000 under Section 80TTA. Senior citizens: up to ₹50,000 under Section 80TTB (senior citizens use 80TTB instead of 80TTA).

Deductions.front: Where in the income‑computation order are Chapter VI‑A deductions (secs 80C–80U) claimed?
Deductions.back: Chapter VI‑A deductions are subtracted from Gross Total Income to arrive at Total Income — claimed after computing Gross Total Income (i.e., post‑aggregation of heads).
Flat ₹75,000; ₹1,25,000 for severe disability (80% or more). 80DD: for a disabled DEPENDANT. 80U: the assessee HIMSELF is disabled. Flat amounts regardless of actual expense. Residents only.

Deductions.front: Common examiner trap: when to apply 80C/other deductions versus exemptions?
Deductions.back: Apply exemptions and compute Gross Total Income first; then deduct Chapter VI‑A (e.g., 80C). Don’t net 80C against individual heads — it reduces Gross Total Income only after aggregation.

Deductions.front: s.80DDB — medical treatment of specified diseases?
Deductions.back: Actual expenditure up to ₹40,000; ₹1,00,000 if the patient is a senior citizen. For self or dependant; reduced by insurance or employer reimbursement.

Deductions.front: s.80G with the 10% qualifying limit — the two steps?
Deductions.back: Step 1: cap the donation at 10% of adjusted gross total income. Step 2: apply 50% or 100% to that capped figure. Cash donations above ₹2,000 get nothing.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: Who must pay advance tax, and who is exempt?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: Anyone whose tax payable for the year is ₹10,000 or more (s.208). Exempt: a RESIDENT individual aged 60+ with no business or professional income (s.207(2)).

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What are the due dates and cumulative instalment percentages for advance‑tax payments?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: 15 June 15%, 15 Sept 45% (cumulative), 15 Dec 75% (cumulative), 15 Mar 100% — standard advance‑tax schedule (instalments of advance tax).

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What is the 234C rule for interest on shortfall in advance instalments?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: 1% per month — interest under s.234C on shortfall in each instalment; charged for the months of deferment on the amount of shortfall for that instalment.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: When is interest under s.234B levied and at what rate?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: 1% per month — s.234B charged from 1 April to date of filing when advance tax paid is insufficient (typically when advance tax paid < 90% of assessed tax).

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: Distinguish s.234A from s.234B (short, buyer’s‑guide answer).
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: 1% p.m. both: s.234A — interest for late filing (from due date to filing) on tax unpaid; s.234B — interest for default in payment of advance tax (from 1 April until filing).
Assessees under s.44AD or s.44ADA pay the whole advance tax in ONE instalment by 15 March. (s.44AE is not covered — normal four instalments.)

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What is the TDS threshold for interest other than on securities (section 194A)?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: ₹50,000 — no TDS under s.194A if interest ≤ ₹50,000 in the year; senior citizens threshold ₹1,00,000 (as notified).

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What is the TDS threshold for professional/technical fees (section 194J)?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: ₹50,000 — TDS under s.194J required when fee/payments in aggregate to a deductee exceed ₹50,000 in the financial year.
Threshold ₹50,000 per MONTH or part of a month (from 1-4-2025; earlier ₹2.4 lakh a year). 10% on land, building, furniture; 2% on plant and machinery — on the whole rent.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What is the TDS threshold for dividend payments (section 194)?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: ₹10,000 — payer must deduct TDS on dividend payments exceeding ₹10,000 in aggregate to a payee in a financial year.
Single payment above ₹30,000 OR aggregate above ₹1,00,000 in the year. 1% if payee is an individual or HUF; 2% for any other payee. On the whole amount.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: s.194T — payments by a firm to its partners?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: From 1-4-2025: 10% TDS on salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest to a partner if the aggregate exceeds ₹20,000 in the year.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: What are the time‑limits for filing belated, revised and updated returns (ss.139(4),(5),(8A))?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: Belated/Revised (ss.139(4)/(5)): by 31 Dec of the assessment year. Updated return (s.139(8A)): within 48 months from end of the relevant assessment year.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: For TDS on salary, what perquisite thresholds for specified employees and medical travel abroad must you remember (Rules 3C/3D)?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: ₹4,00,000 — 'specified employee' salary limit (Rule 3C); ₹8,00,000 gross total income limit for medical travel abroad perquisite (Rule 3D).

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: s.194-IB — rent paid by an individual/HUF not liable to audit?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: Rent above ₹50,000 a month: 2% (cut from 5% on 1-10-2024), deducted once — in the last month of the year or of the tenancy. No TAN needed.
194Q: buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore deducts 0.1% on purchases EXCEEDING ₹50 lakh. 206C(1H) (TCS by seller on goods) was switched off from 1-4-2025.
Threshold ₹10 lakh (from 1-4-2025). Other purposes: 20% on the excess. Education/medical: 5% on the excess. Education funded by a loan from a specified institution: nil.

Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.front: s.194J — which payments attract 2% rather than 10%?
Advance Tax, TDS and TCS.back: Fees for TECHNICAL services, royalty for sale/distribution of films, and call centres: 2%. Professional services, directors' fees and other royalty: 10%. Threshold ₹50,000.

Clubbing of Income.front: When is income of your spouse clubbed in your hands? Give the essential condition and section.
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Income is clubbed when you transfer an asset to your spouse without adequate consideration and income arises from that asset; such income is included in your total income — Section 64(1).

Clubbing of Income.front: When is a minor child's income NOT clubbed u/s 64(1A)?
Clubbing of Income.back: (1) Income from manual work; (2) income from an activity involving the child's skill, talent or specialised knowledge; (3) the minor suffers from a disability specified in s.80U. Everything else is clubbed.

Clubbing of Income.front: What happens to income where you transfer only the income (not the asset) to another person? Name the section.
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Income transferred without transfer of the asset remains taxable in the transferor’s hands — Section 60.

Clubbing of Income.front: When is a revocable transfer treated as clubbed in the transferor's hands? (state the rule concisely)
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. If the transfer is revocable or the transferor retains the right to re-vest the asset/its income, income is treated as transferor’s and clubbed in his total income.

Clubbing of Income.front: How is income treated when an asset is transferred to another but for the benefit (direct/indirect) of the transferor?
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Income arising to the transferee is included in the transferor’s income where the transfer was made for the transferor’s benefit; clubbing applies (provisions of Chapter on clubbing).

Clubbing of Income.front: Minor's income: clubbed with which parent, and what exemption?
Clubbing of Income.back: With the parent whose total income (before clubbing) is HIGHER; if parents are separated, the parent maintaining the child. Exemption u/s 10(32): ₹1,500 per child (old regime only).

Clubbing of Income.front: How are deductions/benefits (e.g., Chapter VI-A) on clubbed income claimed — by transferor or transferee?
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Deductions related to clubbed income are claimed by the transferor (whose total income includes the clubbed amount), subject to usual conditions and limits.

Clubbing of Income.front: Name the single most common computation error students make in clubbing problems.
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Error: taxing clubbed income in transferee’s hands and again in transferor’s—correct: include clubbed income only in transferor’s gross total income for taxation.

Clubbing of Income.front: Does clubbing change the nature (salary/business/capital gains) of the income when included in transferor's hands?
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. No — clubbed income retains its original character (e.g., salary/business/capital gain) when included in the transferor’s total income for computation and reliefs.

Clubbing of Income.front: What's the basic procedural step when you identify a clubbing situation in an exam computation?
Clubbing of Income.back: 1. Step: exclude the clubbed amount from recipient’s taxable income; add that amount to transferor’s appropriate head in his gross total income and compute tax there.

Clubbing of Income.front: Spouse's remuneration from a concern in which the individual has substantial interest?
Clubbing of Income.back: Clubbed with the individual (s.64(1)(ii)) — UNLESS the spouse has technical or professional qualifications and the income is solely attributable to them. Substantial interest = 20% or more.

Clubbing of Income.front: Asset gifted to spouse vs to son's wife?
Clubbing of Income.back: Both clubbed with the transferor (s.64(1)(iv) and (vi)). Exceptions for spouse: transfer for adequate consideration or under an agreement to live apart. Income on the accumulated income is NOT clubbed.
Yes. A gifts to B's wife and B gifts to A's wife: each income is clubbed in the hands of the deemed transferor, to the extent the gifts match.

Return of Income.front: Due dates for the return u/s 139(1)?
Return of Income.back: 31 July: individuals and others not requiring audit. 31 October: companies, audit cases and their partners. 30 November: transfer-pricing cases. (30 September is the tax AUDIT REPORT date, not the return.)

Return of Income.front: What is the last date to file a BELATED or a REVISED return for a year?
Return of Income.back: 31 December of the relevant assessment year — deadline for belated returns (s.139(4)) and revised returns (s.139(5)).

Return of Income.front: What is the time‑limit to file an UPDATED return under section 139(8A)?
Return of Income.back: 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year — maximum period to furnish an updated return u/s 139(8A).

Return of Income.front: Updated return u/s 139(8A) — additional tax by timing?
Return of Income.back: On tax + interest: 25% if filed within 12 months of the end of the AY; 50% within 24; 60% within 36; 70% within 48. Cannot be used to claim a refund, reduce tax or increase a loss.

Return of Income.front: How do you distinguish a BELATED return (s.139(4)) from a REVISED return (s.139(5)) — in one line?
Return of Income.back: Belated: return filed after the due date under s.139(1) (s.139(4)). Revised: return filed to correct an earlier return within the statutory time limit (s.139(5), by 31‑Dec).

Return of Income.front: What filing requirement affects the CARRY‑FORWARD of business or capital losses?
Return of Income.back: File return on or before the due date u/s 139(1) to claim carry‑forward of business or capital losses; belated/revised returns generally disallow carry‑forward (statutory condition).

Return of Income.front: What is the procedure and time‑limit when the AO finds a defect in a return (s.139(9))?
Return of Income.back: 15 days — AO may issue a defect notice u/s 139(9); taxpayer must rectify within the notice period (usually 15 days), failing which the return may be treated as invalid/void (treated as not filed).

Return of Income.front: If a return is treated as INVALID because defects were not rectified, how is a later filing treated?
Return of Income.back: Any subsequent filing is treated as a belated return u/s 139(4) (i.e., treated as filed after the due date).

Return of Income.front: Practical order of remedies if you discover omissions: revise, or update — which to use and when?
Return of Income.back: 1) If within 31‑Dec of AY, file a revised return u/s 139(5). 2) If beyond 31‑Dec but within 48 months, pay tax+interest and file an updated return u/s 139(8A).

Return of Income.front: Fee for filing the return late (s.234F)?
Return of Income.back: ₹5,000; ₹1,000 if total income does not exceed ₹5 lakh. Separate from 1% a month interest u/s 234A.

Return of Income.front: Who must file a return even with income below the exemption limit?
Return of Income.back: Current-account deposits above ₹1 crore; foreign travel spend above ₹2 lakh; electricity above ₹1 lakh; turnover above ₹60 lakh or professional receipts above ₹10 lakh; TDS/TCS ₹25,000+ (₹50,000 seniors); savings deposits ₹50 lakh+.

Return of Income.front: Who verifies the return of a company, firm and LLP (s.140)?
Return of Income.back: Company: managing director (else any director). Firm: managing partner (else any partner not a minor). LLP: designated partner. Individual: himself, or a duly authorised person if absent or incapacitated.

Computation of Total Income.front: Which five heads must you add to arrive at Gross Total Income (name with sections)?
Computation of Total Income.back: 5: Salaries (s.15–17), House Property (s.22–27), PGBP (s.28–44), Capital Gains (s.45–55A), Other Sources (s.56–59).

Computation of Total Income.front: Give the exact stepwise sequence from heads of income to tax payable (brief steps you must follow in exam).
Computation of Total Income.back: 6-step sequence: (1) Compute each head; (2) Aggregate = Gross Total Income; (3) Deduct Chapter VI‑A (s.80) → Total Income; (4) Compute tax on Total Income (apply rebate); (5) Add surcharge (if any); (6) Add cess 4%.

Computation of Total Income.front: What is the standard deduction for salary under old and new regimes (amount and where claimed)?
Computation of Total Income.back: ₹50,000 old regime; ₹75,000 new regime — allowable against Salary income (practical deduction from gross salary) when taxpayer opts respective regime (salary deductions under s.16/assessment rules).

Computation of Total Income.front: New regime slabs for AY 2026-27 — and the cumulative tax at each step?
How much extra NPS deduction is allowed under 80CCD(1B) and who can claim it?
Computation of Total Income.back: ₹50,000 additional under s.80CCD(1B): available to individual taxpayers (employee or self‑employed) over and above s.80C limit; NPS Vatsalya (minor account) eligible within this ₹50,000.

Computation of Total Income.front: State the tax treatment and thresholds for capital gains on listed equity/units (STT‑paid): LTCG, STCG and other LTCG rates/thresholds.
Computation of Total Income.back: ₹1,25,000 exemption threshold for LTCG (s.112A): LTCG taxed at 12.5% on amount above ₹1.25 lakh. STCG on STT‑paid equity taxed under s.111A at 20%. Other LTCG taxed 12.5% (no indexation).

Computation of Total Income.front: How may capital losses be set off and carried forward? (short‑term v long‑term capital losses)
Computation of Total Income.back: STCL: set off against any capital gains; LTCL: set off only against LTCG (s.74). Carry forward: capital losses eligible for 8 assessment years (carry forward under s.74), set off per same restrictions.

Computation of Total Income.front: What is the mandatory order of set‑off when you have losses and incomes across heads? (single exam trap)
Computation of Total Income.back: Order: intra‑head set‑off first (losses among sources within same head), then inter‑head set‑off across heads (s.70). Always exhaust intra‑head before inter‑head adjustments.

Computation of Total Income.front: Marginal relief just above ₹12 lakh (new regime)?
Computation of Total Income.back: Tax cannot exceed the income above ₹12,00,000. E.g. income ₹12,10,000: slab tax ₹61,500 but payable ₹10,000 (+ cess). Without it, earning ₹10,000 more would cost ₹61,500.

Computation of Total Income.front: Is the s.87A rebate available against tax on capital gains u/s 111A/112A in the new regime?
Computation of Total Income.back: No (from AY 2026-27). The rebate is limited to tax at SLAB rates. So total income under ₹12 lakh can still carry tax if it includes special-rate income.

Computation of Total Income.front: State the Chapter VI‑A deduction point: from which aggregate are s.80 deductions allowed and cite section.
Computation of Total Income.back: From Gross Total Income: Chapter VI‑A deductions (s.80 onwards) are claimed after aggregating all heads to arrive at Gross Total Income, reducing it to Total Income (s.80).

Computation of Total Income.front: Give the rebate under section 87A for new regime and state old‑regime figure (limits and amounts).
Computation of Total Income.back: New regime rebate (s.87A): up to ₹12,00,000 total income, rebate capped at ₹60,000 (with marginal relief). Old regime unchanged: rebate for incomes up to ₹5,00,000 — max ₹12,500 (prior notified limit).

Computation of Total Income.front: Surcharge rates for an individual — and the new-regime cap?
Computation of Total Income.back: 10% above ₹50 lakh; 15% above ₹1 crore; 25% above ₹2 crore; 37% above ₹5 crore (old regime only). New regime caps at 25%. On dividend and 111A/112/112A gains: max 15%.
₹2,50,000 general; ₹3,00,000 resident aged 60 to under 80; ₹5,00,000 resident aged 80+. The NEW regime has one limit of ₹4,00,000 for everyone.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: Which section levies CGST on intra‑State supplies — state of supply and the exact legal provision you must quote in answers?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Section 9 CGST Act: CGST is levied on all intra‑State supplies of goods or services as per rates notified under the Act (levy of CGST — s.9).

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: Which section levies IGST — when is IGST chargeable (states of movement/import)?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Section 5 IGST Act: IGST is levied on all inter‑State supplies and on supplies in the course of import of goods or services; IGST applies when supply crosses State/Union border or at import clearance.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: What is the statutory test and key inclusions of 'supply' that you must cite in answers?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Section 7 GST Act: Supply = sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal for a consideration, made in course/ furtherance of business; includes imports, deemed supplies and specified activities.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: CGST + SGST or IGST — the one decisive test?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Compare the LOCATION OF THE SUPPLIER with the PLACE OF SUPPLY (not the recipient's location). Same State: intra-State, CGST + SGST. Different States: inter-State, IGST. Imports: IGST.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: How does GST treat a composite supply versus a mixed supply — which rate applies?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Composite v mixed: Composite supply charged at rate of the principal (dominant) supply; Mixed supply charged at the highest rate applicable to any component (classic examiner trap).

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: What are the monetary eligibility limits for opting composition scheme?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Turnover limit: aggregate annual turnover up to ₹1.50 crore (₹75 lakh for special category States) — Section 10 (composition) eligibility threshold.

Makers of inter-State outward supplies; suppliers through an e-commerce operator liable to TCS; manufacturers of ice cream, pan masala, tobacco, aerated waters; casual and non-resident taxable persons; suppliers of non-taxable goods.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: What are the three core consequences of opting for composition you must state in answers?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: Consequences: (1) pay tax at notified concessional rate under s.10, (2) cannot collect tax from recipient, (3) cannot claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) on purchases.

Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).front: Reverse charge u/s 9(3) — the services to remember?
Charge of GST (Levy, Composition, RCM).back: GTA (5%, recipient pays); legal services by an advocate to a business entity; director's services to the company; sponsorship to a body corporate or firm; residential dwelling rented to a registered person; security services by a non-corporate to a registered person.
Manufacturers: 1% of turnover in the State. Traders: 1% of turnover of TAXABLE supplies. Restaurants: 5%. Service providers u/s 10(2A): 6%, turnover up to ₹50 lakh. (CGST + SGST combined.)

9(3): NOTIFIED goods/services — recipient pays whatever the supplier's status. 9(4): specified registered recipients (promoters in real estate) pay on notified supplies received from UNREGISTERED suppliers.

Introduction to GST.front: State the GST rate slabs after GST 2.0 and which slabs were abolished (give effective date).
Introduction to GST.back: 3 slabs: 5%, 18%, 40% (effective 22‑Sep‑2025); 12% and 28% abolished; individual health and life insurance made exempt under GST 2.0.

Introduction to GST.front: What is the basic rule for when GST is leviable (scope of levy)?
Introduction to GST.back: Rule: GST is leviable on any 'supply' of goods or services for consideration made in India by a taxable person, except supplies notified as exempt; exports are zero‑rated.

Introduction to GST.front: What does 'supply' cover under GST — give the short statutory list of examples.
Introduction to GST.back: Section 7: 'supply' includes sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease, disposal, or import of services, and activities treated as supply even without consideration.

Introduction to GST.front: How is a composite supply taxed versus a mixed supply — what common examiner trap must you avoid?
Introduction to GST.back: Rule: composite supply taxed at the rate of the principal supply; mixed supply taxed at the highest rate applicable to any component (don’t confuse 'principal' with 'highest‑rate').

Introduction to GST.front: GST Council — voting weights, majority and quorum?
Introduction to GST.back: Centre one-third, all States together two-thirds. Decisions need three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting. Quorum: half the members. Chair: Union Finance Minister (Art. 279A).

Introduction to GST.front: Which Articles: power to levy GST, IGST on inter-State supply, GST Council?
Introduction to GST.back: 246A: concurrent power of Parliament and States to make GST laws. 269A: levy and apportionment of IGST on inter-State supplies and imports. 279A: GST Council. 366(12A): definition of GST.

Introduction to GST.front: List the conditions required to claim Input Tax Credit (one‑line mnemonic).
Introduction to GST.back: 5 conditions: (1) registered person, (2) tax invoice/debit note, (3) receipt of goods/services, (4) tax charged and paid by supplier, (5) return filed — Section 16.

Introduction to GST.front: What happens if the recipient does NOT pay the supplier within 180 days of the invoice?
Introduction to GST.back: 180 days: recipient must reverse any ITC availed (plus interest) if payment to the supplier is not made within 180 days of invoice; reversed ITC treated as output tax.

Introduction to GST.front: By what deadline must credit‑note adjustments and related ITC be recorded (statutory cut‑off)?
Introduction to GST.back: 30 November following the financial year: credit notes (s.34) and ITC adjustments (s.16(4)) must be recorded/claimed by this date.

Introduction to GST.front: State the current GST TDS and e‑commerce TCS rates and the TDS applicability threshold.
Introduction to GST.back: TDS s.51: 2% where contract value exceeds ₹2.5 lakh; TCS s.52 (e‑commerce operators): 0.5% on supplies collected by the operator.

Alcoholic liquor for human consumption (States tax it). Five petroleum products — crude, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas — until the Council recommends a date. Electricity. Tobacco is IN GST and can also bear excise.

Supply under GST.front: State precisely what 'supply' includes under GST (mention section/schedules).
Supply under GST.back: 1. Section 7: 'supply' includes goods/services for consideration in course or furtherance of business; import of services for consideration; activities in Schedule I deemed supply; Schedule II classifies; Schedule III items are not supplies.

Supply under GST.front: Which transactions are treated as 'supply' even without consideration? Give classic Schedule I examples.
Supply under GST.back: 1. Schedule I: supply between related/distinct persons without consideration; transfer/disposal of business assets on cessation; supply of goods by principal to agent — all treated as 'supply' even when no consideration.

Supply under GST.front: Under Schedule II, how is a works contract treated for GST purposes?
Supply under GST.back: 1. Schedule II: a works contract is treated as a 'supply of service' (i.e., taxable as service, not as sale of goods).

Supply under GST.front: Name two transactions that are explicitly NOT supplies under GST (Schedule III).
Supply under GST.back: 1. Schedule III: services by an employee to employer; sale of land and sale of (completed) buildings — are treated as neither supply of goods nor services.

Supply under GST.front: Define 'composite supply' and state the tax rule that applies (mention section).
Supply under GST.back: 1. Section 2(30): composite supply = two or more supplies naturally bundled with a principal supply; entire composite is taxed at the rate of the principal supply.

Supply under GST.front: Define 'mixed supply' and state the tax rule that applies (mention section).
Supply under GST.back: 1. Section 2(74): mixed supply = two or more supplies packaged together not naturally bundled; taxed at the highest rate applicable to any component.

Supply under GST.front: Is import of services taxable under GST even if not in course/furtherance of business? Quote the section.
Supply under GST.back: 1. Section 7(1)(b): Yes — import of services for consideration is treated as 'supply' and taxable whether or not in course or furtherance of business.

Supply under GST.front: When deciding whether a transaction is a 'supply', what is the primary test and its key exceptions?
Supply under GST.back: 1. Primary test: 'in course or furtherance of business' (Section 7). Key exceptions: Schedule I transactions, import of services, and supplies between related/distinct persons (treated as supply even without consideration).

Supply under GST.front: If a composite supply contains exempt, zero-rated and taxable elements, which tax rate applies to the invoice?
Supply under GST.back: 1. Rule: The tax rate of the principal supply applies to the entire composite — even if other components are exempt or zero-rated.

Supply under GST.front: How are supplies between distinct persons (separately registered branches) treated for GST?
Supply under GST.back: 1. Rule: Supplies between distinct persons (separately registered branches) are taxable supplies — treated as supplies (inter- or intra-state as per place of supply rules).

Place of Supply.front: Inter-State or intra-State — what is compared?
Place of Supply.back: Location of the SUPPLIER and the PLACE OF SUPPLY. Different States: inter-State (IGST, s.7 IGST Act). Same State: intra-State (CGST + SGST, s.8). The recipient's location matters only where the rule makes it the place of supply.

Place of Supply.front: Goods involving movement — place of supply? And bill-to ship-to?
Place of Supply.back: s.10(1)(a): where the movement TERMINATES for delivery to the recipient. s.10(1)(b): delivered on the direction of a THIRD PERSON → that third person's principal place of business.

Place of Supply.front: Goods with no movement, and goods assembled or installed at site?
Place of Supply.back: No movement: location of the goods at the time of delivery (s.10(1)(c)). Assembled/installed: place of installation (s.10(1)(d)). On board a conveyance: where taken on board (s.10(1)(e)).

Place of Supply.front: What is the place of supply for goods supplied on board a conveyance (e.g., food sold on a train)?
Place of Supply.back: Location at which the goods are taken on board the conveyance (place where goods are loaded/embarked).

Place of Supply.front: Default rule for services, both parties in India (s.12(2))?
Place of Supply.back: To a REGISTERED person: location of the recipient. To an UNREGISTERED person: location of the recipient if his address is on record; otherwise location of the supplier.

Place of Supply.front: Where is the place of supply for services related to immovable property (including short‑stay accommodation)?
Place of Supply.back: Location where the immovable property is situated (includes rentals, construction, architect, surveying, and short‑term accommodation).

Place of Supply.front: For admission to events or supplying event‑services, where is the place of supply?
Place of Supply.back: Location where the event actually takes place (the physical venue where the event is held).
Registered recipient: location of the recipient. Unregistered: place where the passenger EMBARKS for a continuous journey (s.12(9)).

Place of Supply.front: Where is the place of supply for transportation of goods (B2C) when someone hires transport?
Place of Supply.back: Location where the goods are handed over for transportation; if B2B, use recipient’s location under the B2B rule.

Place of Supply.front: How to locate place of supply for restaurant, catering and food‑service supplies?
Place of Supply.back: Place where the services are actually performed — the physical location of the restaurant or catering venue.

Place of Supply.front: Training/performance appraisal, and banking services — place of supply?
Place of Supply.back: Training (s.12(5)): registered recipient → his location; unregistered → where actually performed. Banking (s.12(12)): location of the recipient on the supplier's records, else location of the supplier.

Place of Supply.front: How do you treat composite and mixed supplies when finding place of supply?
Place of Supply.back: Composite: place of supply = place of the principal supply. Mixed: treat each component separately and determine place for each supply.

Time of Supply.front: Advance received: is GST payable at receipt — goods vs services?
Time of Supply.back: SERVICES: yes, time of supply is the earlier of invoice and payment, so an advance is taxed on receipt (receipt voucher). GOODS: no tax on advances — time of supply is the invoice date or last date to invoice.

Time of Supply.front: When is the time of supply for a single‑purpose voucher and for a multi‑purpose voucher?
Time of Supply.back: Single‑purpose: date of sale/issue of the voucher (taxable on issue). Multi‑purpose: date of voucher redemption (taxable on redemption).

Time of Supply.front: By what time must a supplier issue a tax invoice for services (deadline)?
Time of Supply.back: 30 days from date of supply of services — invoice must be issued within 30 days, failing which time‑of‑supply consequences apply.

Time of Supply.front: When must a tax invoice for goods be issued (timing relative to removal/delivery)?
Time of Supply.back: Before or at the time of removal/delivery of goods for supply — invoice must accompany or precede physical movement/delivery.

Time of Supply.front: What is the 'date of receipt of payment'?
Time of Supply.back: The EARLIER of the date it is entered in the supplier's books and the date it is credited to his bank account (Explanation to s.12/13).

Time of Supply.front: Time of supply of GOODS under forward charge?
Time of Supply.back: Earlier of (a) date of issue of invoice and (b) the last date on which the invoice was required to be issued u/s 31. Date of payment is not relevant for goods.

Time of Supply.front: How is time of supply determined for continuous supplies with periodic billing?
Time of Supply.back: Earliest of: date of issue of periodic invoice, date of receipt of payment for that period, or the date on which supplier becomes entitled to issue the invoice for that period.

Time of Supply.front: If an invoice for services is not issued within the prescribed 30 days, what becomes the time of supply?
Time of Supply.back: Date of provision of the service — if invoice isn’t issued within 30 days, the service date (or earlier payment date) becomes the tax point.

Time of Supply.front: By when must credit or debit notes be issued to adjust output tax/ITC for a financial year?
Time of Supply.back: 30 November following the end of the financial year — deadline for issuing credit/debit notes under s.34 and for ITC adjustments under s.16(4).

Time of Supply.front: Reverse charge — time of supply for goods and for services?
Time of Supply.back: Goods (s.12(3)): earliest of receipt of goods, date of payment, 30 days from supplier's invoice. Services (s.13(3)): earlier of date of payment and 60 days from invoice. Payment date = earlier of books entry and bank debit.

Time of Supply.front: Change in rate of tax (s.14) — the rule of thumb?
Time of Supply.back: Three events: supply, invoice, payment. The rate in force when ANY TWO of them occur applies. Supplied before the change but invoiced and paid after → new rate, time of supply = earlier of invoice/payment.

Value of Supply.front: What is the primary legal basis for determining the value of a taxable supply in GST exams?
Value of Supply.back: Section 15: Transaction value (price actually paid or payable) is the primary basis for value of supply, subject to specified inclusions, exclusions and exceptions under the Act.

Value of Supply.front: When must the transaction value be set aside and GST Valuation Rules applied instead?
Value of Supply.back: Section 15: When supplier and recipient are related or price is influenced by special relationship/conditions, transaction value may be disregarded and Valuation Rules applied in prescribed order.

Value of Supply.front: What must be ADDED to transaction value (s.15(2))?
Value of Supply.back: Non-GST taxes and duties; amounts the SUPPLIER was liable to pay but the recipient incurred; incidental expenses (packing, commission) charged before delivery; interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment; subsidies linked to price EXCEPT government subsidies.

Value of Supply.front: When can a discount be excluded from taxable value without a credit note?
Value of Supply.back: Section 15: Discounts given before or at time of supply and specifically recorded in invoice/contract are excluded from value; post‑supply discounts must be adjusted by credit note to reduce taxable value.

Value of Supply.front: Deadline for a credit note to reduce output tax?
Value of Supply.back: 30 November following the financial year of the supply, or the annual return date, whichever is earlier (s.34(2)). A credit note can be issued any time; this limit only governs the tax adjustment.

Value of Supply.front: What conditions must be satisfied for a reimbursement to be excluded as a 'pure agent' (not part of value)?
Value of Supply.back: Pure agent (valuation rules): Excluded if supplier acts on recipient's directions, pays third party, recovers exact amount without markup, separately shown on invoice and supported by documents.

Value of Supply.front: Is GST/IGST/UTGST/Compensation Cess charged by supplier included in the taxable value?
Value of Supply.back: Excluded: Taxes levied under GST (CGST/IGST/UTGST/compensation cess) charged by supplier are not part of taxable value (Section 15).

Value of Supply.front: How is consideration paid or payable by a third party treated for GST valuation?
Value of Supply.back: Included: Any consideration paid or payable by a third party for supply is part of the value and must be included in taxable value (Section 15).

Value of Supply.front: How is consideration 'not wholly in money' treated for valuation?
Value of Supply.back: Money‑equivalent: Non‑monetary consideration is valued at its money equivalent and included in taxable value (Section 15).

Value of Supply.front: What is the examiner‑safe order of steps to compute taxable value (common mistake to avoid)?
Value of Supply.back: Steps: 1) establish transaction value (Section 15); 2) exclude allowable pre‑supply discounts/pure‑agent amounts; 3) add includible expenses/third‑party consideration; 4) apply Valuation Rules if transaction value not acceptable.

Value of Supply.front: Post-supply discount — when is it deductible from value?
Value of Supply.back: s.15(3)(b): only if (1) established by an agreement entered into at or BEFORE the time of supply and linked to specific invoices, AND (2) the recipient has reversed the proportionate ITC. A spontaneous later discount gets nothing.

Exemptions from GST.front: List the three legal categories of supplies that result in no GST (name the statutes).
Exemptions from GST.back: 3 categories: zero‑rated supplies (IGST Act s.16), exempt/nil‑rated supplies (by notification under CGST Act s.11) and non‑GST activities (Schedule III, CGST Act).

Exemptions from GST.front: Define zero‑rated supply and the two routes available for exporters.
Exemptions from GST.back: Zero‑rated = exports and supplies to SEZ (IGST Act s.16). 2 routes: export under LUT without tax; or pay IGST and claim refund of unutilised ITC.

Exemptions from GST.front: What is the immediate ITC consequence when you make an exempt (nil‑rated) supply?
Exemptions from GST.back: 0 output tax collected; inputs/services used exclusively for exempt supplies disallow ITC. Common inputs require proportionate reversal under CGST s.17 and Rules 42/43.

Exemptions from GST.front: When is a composite supply treated as exempt?
Exemptions from GST.back: When the principal supply is exempt, the entire composite supply is exempt. Always determine the principal supply first (composite‑supply principle).

Exemptions from GST.front: How is a mixed supply taxed if one component is exempt?
Exemptions from GST.back: Tax at the highest rate among components (mixed‑supply rule). If one component is exempt, highest taxable component’s rate applies.

Exemptions from GST.front: Give three Schedule III examples that are treated as 'not a supply' for GST.
Exemptions from GST.back: 3 examples: sale of land; actionable claims (except lottery/Betting where taxable); services by an employee to employer (also services of courts). (Schedule III, CGST Act).

Exemptions from GST.front: What must an exporter furnish to supply zero‑rated under LUT and consequence if not furnished?
Exemptions from GST.back: 1 valid LUT before export. If no LUT furnished, exporter must pay IGST on export and then claim refund; LUT avoids upfront tax payment.

Exemptions from GST.front: What monthly reversal/reporting must be done in GSTR‑3B because of exempt supplies?
Exemptions from GST.back: Monthly: proportionate ITC reversal for exempt supplies must be reported in GSTR‑3B using Rule 42/43; reversal increases output tax liability for the month.
From 22-9-2025: INDIVIDUAL life insurance and INDIVIDUAL health insurance policies are exempt. Group policies are not covered by this exemption.

Exemptions from GST.front: Exam trap: difference between 'exempt' and 'zero‑rated' regarding availability of ITC refund?
Exemptions from GST.back: Key: Zero‑rated allows refund of unutilised ITC (LUT or IGST+refund). Exempt/nil‑rated does NOT permit refund of ITC — ITC must be reversed or cannot be claimed.
Health care services by a clinical establishment are exempt, EXCEPT room charges above ₹5,000 per day (other than ICU/CCU/ICCU/NICU), which are taxable without ITC.

Exemptions from GST.front: Renting a residential dwelling — exempt or taxable?
Exemptions from GST.back: Exempt when used as a residence — EXCEPT when let to a registered person, who then pays under reverse charge. Still exempt if the registered person is a proprietor renting it for his own residence in a personal capacity.

Services by an educational institution (pre-school to higher secondary, recognised qualifications, approved vocational courses) to students, faculty and staff. Private coaching is taxable. Catering/transport/security exempt only up to higher secondary.

Exemptions from GST.front: Passenger transport — which modes are exempt?
Exemptions from GST.back: Non-AC contract carriage (not tourism/charter), non-AC stage carriage, metro/monorail/tram, inland waterways, rail other than first class and AC. Taxable: air, AC bus, radio taxi, AC and first-class rail.

Input Tax Credit.front: What is the last date to claim ITC on invoices/credit notes for a financial year (normal rule)?
Input Tax Credit.back: 30 November following the financial year — final cutoff to avail ITC/adjust with credit notes (s.16(4); credit notes s.34).

Input Tax Credit.front: If a recipient fails to pay the supplier within how many days must ITC be reversed?
Input Tax Credit.back: 180 days — ITC must be reversed if recipient doesn’t pay supplier the invoice value within 180 days of invoice (s.16(2)); reversed amount attracts interest (s.50).

Input Tax Credit.front: What is the interest rate applicable on ITC reversed (and later not restored)?
Input Tax Credit.back: 18% per annum — interest under s.50 on amount of ITC reversed/short-paid, calculated from date of availing credit to reversal date (s.50 CGST).

Input Tax Credit.front: Name five classic ‘blocked credits’ (numeric rule reference and examples).
Input Tax Credit.back: Section 17(5) — major blocked items: motor vehicles, food/refreshments, club memberships, works contract for immovable property, personal consumption; these credits are not admissible (s.17(5)).

Input Tax Credit.front: Motor vehicles (seating up to 13) — when is ITC allowed despite s.17(5)?
Input Tax Credit.back: When used for (i) further supply of such vehicles, (ii) transportation of passengers, or (iii) imparting training on driving. Vehicles for transport of GOODS are not blocked at all.

Input Tax Credit.front: ITC on capital goods when moving from composition/exempt to taxable (s.18)?
Input Tax Credit.back: Credit is reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter or part from the invoice date (Rule 40). New registrants u/s 18(1)(a)/(b) get credit only on INPUTS in stock, not capital goods. Invoice must not be over 1 year old.

Input Tax Credit.front: Is IGST paid on import of goods eligible as ITC; what about basic customs duty?
Input Tax Credit.back: IGST on import — eligible as ITC; basic customs duty — not eligible. (Import IGST credit allowed under ITC provisions; BCD excluded.)

Input Tax Credit.front: Can a recipient claim ITC on tax paid under reverse charge mechanism (RCM)?
Input Tax Credit.back: Yes — ITC for tax paid under RCM is available provided recipient has tax invoice, goods/services received and files the return/pay tax; treat like other ITC (s.16 conditions apply).

Input Tax Credit.front: Common credit used for taxable and exempt supplies — how apportioned?
Input Tax Credit.back: s.17(2) with Rule 42: reverse common credit × exempt turnover ÷ total turnover. Capital goods: Rule 43, spread over 60 months.

Input Tax Credit.front: If a credit note is issued in the next financial year, by when must it be issued to adjust ITC for the earlier FY?
Input Tax Credit.back: 30 November following the financial year — credit notes affecting ITC for a FY must be issued by that date to adjust the earlier year’s ITC (s.34; s.16(4)).

Tax invoice or debit note in hand; invoice furnished by the supplier and reflected in GSTR-2B; goods/services received; tax actually paid to Government; recipient has filed GSTR-3B. No provisional credit beyond GSTR-2B.

Input Tax Credit.front: s.17(5)(b) — food, catering, health, insurance: the exception?
Input Tax Credit.back: Blocked unless (a) used for making an outward supply of the same category, or (b) OBLIGATORY for the employer to provide to employees under any law — e.g. a canteen required by the Factories Act.

Input Tax Credit.front: Banks and NBFCs — the s.17(4) option?
Input Tax Credit.back: Either normal apportionment u/s 17(2), or avail 50% of eligible ITC every month and let the rest lapse. Option cannot be withdrawn during the rest of the financial year.

Registration.front: Within how many days must a person apply for GST registration after becoming liable to register?
Registration.back: 30 days — apply within 30 days from the date you become liable to register (Section 25, CGST Act).

Registration.front: How many days before commencement of business must a casual or non‑resident taxable person apply for GST registration?
