Registration.back: 5 days — apply at least 5 days before commencing business, with advance deposit of estimated tax (provisions under Section 25 and GST Rules for casual/non‑resident taxable persons).

Registration.front: How many GST registrations are required if a taxpayer has business locations in multiple States/UTs?
Registration.back: One per State/UT — separate GST registration is required for each State or Union Territory where business is carried on (separate registrations per State/UT).

Registration.front: What is the format and component breakdown of a GSTIN?
Registration.back: 15 characters — 2‑digit State code + 10‑character PAN + 13th‑character entity number (same PAN) + 14th default ‘Z’ + 15th check‑digit (GSTIN structure).

Registration.front: Is PAN mandatory for GST registration? Any exception?
Registration.back: PAN mandatory — PAN is required for registration; exception: where PAN is not available (non‑resident applicants) other prescribed documents may be allowed per rules.

Registration.front: Can a person below the GST turnover threshold obtain registration voluntarily?
Registration.back: Yes — voluntary registration permitted regardless of turnover; once registered, all compliances, tax liabilities and returns apply (voluntary registration allowed).

Registration.front: Within how many days must changes in registration particulars be intimated to the tax authority?
Registration.back: 15 days — notify and amend registration particulars within 15 days of any change (amendment of registration under GST Rules).

Registration.front: What does the 13th character of the GSTIN signify?
Registration.back: Entity number — 13th character denotes the number of registrations (entity) with the same PAN in that State (1 for first registration, 2 for second, etc.).

Registration.front: Several places of business in ONE State — how many registrations?
Registration.back: One is enough, but a SEPARATE registration may be taken for each place of business (s.25(2)). Establishments with separate registrations are 'distinct persons' — supplies between them are taxable.

Registration.front: From which date is GST registration effective when an application is filed late or on time?
Registration.back: Effective date rule — if application is within 30 days, registration effective from date liability arose; if later, registration effective from date of grant (Section 25, CGST Act).
₹40 lakh: exclusively GOODS, in States that adopted it. ₹20 lakh: services or mixed. ₹10 lakh: Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura. The ₹40 lakh limit is not for ice cream, pan masala, tobacco.
All taxable supplies + exempt supplies + exports + inter-State supplies, all-India, same PAN. EXCLUDES inward supplies under reverse charge and the GST itself.

Inter-State taxable supply of GOODS; casual and non-resident taxable persons; those paying under reverse charge; e-commerce operators and their suppliers (with relaxations); TDS deductors; agents. Inter-State SERVICES get the threshold.

Registration.front: Casual taxable person — validity of registration?
Registration.back: Period in the application or 90 days, whichever is earlier; extendable by up to 90 days. Advance deposit of estimated tax required. Apply at least 5 days before starting.
Apply within 90 days of service of the cancellation order (was 30); extendable by up to 180 days by the Commissioner. Not available for voluntary cancellation.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: By when must a supplier issue a tax invoice for (a) goods and (b) services? Quote section.
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Goods: before or at time of removal/delivery; Services: within 30 days from date of supply. Section 31(2).

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: Give the essential mandatory particulars that must appear on every tax invoice (name the section).
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Section 31(2) — invoice number & date; supplier & recipient name, address, GSTIN; HSN/SAC; description, qty, value; taxable value; rate & tax amount; place of supply; signatory.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: When is a bill of supply issued instead of a tax invoice?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: By a composition taxpayer, and for EXEMPT supplies (s.31(3)(c)). Exports are zero-rated and need a tax invoice, not a bill of supply.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: Who issues credit and debit notes and for what events? Quote the governing section.
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Section 34 — Supplier issues Credit Note for decrease in taxable value/tax; Supplier issues Debit Note for increase in taxable value/tax; must reference original invoice and reason.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: What is the last date to issue a credit/debit note so the recipient can claim/adjust ITC? Cite sections.
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: 30 November following the end of the financial year in which supply was made, or date of filing annual return, whichever is earlier. Sections 34 and 16(4).

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: If a credit note is issued in October, when must supplier and recipient reflect it in GST returns? (month-wise action).
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Supplier: declare CN in returns for the month when CN issued (October). Recipient: reduce/reverse ITC in return for the same tax period (October). Sections 34 & 16(4).

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: Name 5 mandatory particulars that must appear on a credit or debit note (section).
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Section 34 — original invoice no & date; CN/DN no & date; value change; tax amount change; reason for issuance; supplier & recipient details.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: Credit note vs debit note — is there a time limit?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Credit note: output tax can be reduced only if declared by 30 November after the FY (or annual return, if earlier). Debit note: no time limit to issue; ITC on it runs from the financial year of the DEBIT NOTE, not the original invoice.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: If a debit note increases taxable value, when must the supplier pay the additional tax and report it?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Additional tax is payable and must be declared in the tax period when the debit note is issued; supplier reports and pays tax in that return. Section 34.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: What must a credit note reference and why is that reference exam-important?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Must reference original invoice number & date — this links adjustment to original supply so CN/DN can alter supplier's output tax and recipient's ITC correctly. Section 34.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: Invoice time limits — banks/insurers, and continuous supply of services?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Services: 30 days from supply; 45 days for banks, insurers, NBFCs. Continuous supply: on or before the due date of payment, or on receipt of payment, or on completion of the event.

Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.front: How many copies of a tax invoice?
Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes.back: Goods: TRIPLICATE — original for recipient, duplicate for transporter, triplicate for supplier. Services: DUPLICATE — original for recipient, duplicate for supplier.

Revised invoice: within one month of the registration certificate, for supplies from the effective date. No invoice needed for supplies under ₹200 to an unregistered person who does not ask — one consolidated invoice at day end.

Accounts and Records.front: How long must a registered person preserve GST accounts and records for a FY?
Accounts and Records.back: 72 months — s.36 CGST Act: preserve for 6 years from the due date of furnishing the annual return for the year to which the accounts relate.

Accounts and Records.front: Which core records must every registered person keep under GST (one‑line list)?
Accounts and Records.back: s.35 — Maintain tax invoices, credit/debit notes, bills of supply, delivery challans, purchase/sales registers, stock accounts, input/output tax ledgers and other prescribed records.

Accounts and Records.front: Can GST books and records be maintained electronically and are they admissible?
Accounts and Records.back: s.35 — Yes: electronic records permitted; must be readable, retained for the prescribed period and produced to the proper officer on demand.

Accounts and Records.front: Does the 6‑year (72‑month) preservation period apply to casual and non‑resident taxable persons?
Accounts and Records.back: 72 months — s.36: yes; applies equally to casual and non‑resident taxable persons, counted from the due date of the annual return for the relevant year.

Accounts and Records.front: What minimum records must an Input Service Distributor (ISD) keep for GST purposes?
Accounts and Records.back: s.35 — ISD must retain invoices received, records of ITC distributed, allocation particulars and recipient details, preserved for the statutory period.

Accounts and Records.front: If an assessment or appeal is pending, how long must related GST records be retained?
Accounts and Records.back: Until final disposal — s.36: retain relevant records beyond 72 months while any assessment, appeal or other proceeding subsists until final disposal.

Accounts and Records.front: What minimum particulars must a tax invoice/record include for GST bookkeeping?
Accounts and Records.back: s.31/s.35 — GSTIN, invoice number/date, supplier and recipient name, HSN/SAC, taxable value, rate, tax amount and place of supply (if interstate).

Accounts and Records.front: What records must an e‑commerce operator maintain for GST and TCS compliance?
Accounts and Records.back: s.35 — Maintain records of supplies made through the platform, supplier details, transaction value, tax collected/settlements and TCS-related documents; preserve for the statutory period.

Accounts and Records.front: Who must keep records even if unregistered?
Accounts and Records.back: Owners/operators of warehouses and godowns, and transporters (s.35(2)); they enrol in GST ENR-01. Records are kept at the principal place of business.

Accounts and Records.front: Annual reconciliation — who certifies GSTR-9C now?
Accounts and Records.back: Self-certified by the taxpayer, where aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore. Audit by a chartered or cost accountant was removed from FY 2020-21.

E-way Bill.front: What consignment value triggers mandatory e‑way bill generation under GST? Cite the rule.
E-way Bill.back: ₹50,000: e‑way bill required where aggregate consignment value exceeds ₹50,000 — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: Who may generate an e‑way bill and when must it be generated?
E-way Bill.back: Supplier, recipient or transporter: e‑way bill must be generated before commencement of movement of goods — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: What information is captured in Part A and Part B of the e‑way bill and who fills each part?
E-way Bill.back: Part A (goods/supply details) by supplier/recipient; Part B (transport/vehicle details) by transporter — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: Which documents must physically accompany the goods during transit under e‑way bill rules?
E-way Bill.back: Invoice or bill of supply/delivery challan and the e‑way bill (or the EWB number) must be carried during transit — Rule 138(7), CGST Rules.
One day for every 200 km or part thereof (normal cargo). Over-dimensional cargo: one day for every 20 km. A 'day' ends at midnight of the day after generation.

E-way Bill.front: Within what time and on what condition can an e‑way bill be cancelled on the portal?
E-way Bill.back: 24 hours: e‑way bill may be cancelled on the portal within 24 hours of generation if goods have not been transported — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: Does e‑way bill requirement apply when goods move for reasons other than supply (job‑work, return, repair, exhibition)?
E-way Bill.back: Yes: if consignment value exceeds ₹50,000, e‑way bill is required even for movements for reasons other than supply (job‑work, return, repair, exhibition etc.) — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: Can a transporter generate a single e‑way bill for multiple consignments carried in the same vehicle?
E-way Bill.back: Yes: transporter may generate a consolidated e‑way bill for multiple consignments carried in one vehicle — Rule 138, CGST Rules.

E-way Bill.front: When is Part B (vehicle details) not required?
E-way Bill.back: Movement within the State of up to 50 km between the consignor's place and the transporter's place (or transporter to consignee). Part A is still needed.

E-way Bill.front: When is no e-way bill required at all?
E-way Bill.back: Consignment value up to ₹50,000 (with exceptions); transport by non-motorised conveyance; goods from port/airport to an ICD or CFS for customs clearance; notified exempt goods.

E-way Bill.front: Acceptance or rejection by the recipient?
E-way Bill.back: Within 72 hours of the details being made available, or the time of delivery, whichever is earlier — else deemed accepted.

TDS and TCS under GST.front: State the GST TDS rate and the value threshold that triggers TDS (section).
TDS and TCS under GST.back: 2% under s.51; applies where contract/payment for taxable supply exceeds ₹2,50,000 (threshold for deduction).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: TCS by e-commerce operators — rate and base?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: 0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST, or 0.5% IGST) of the NET value of taxable supplies made through the operator — reduced from 1% with effect from 10 July 2024 (s.52).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: Who is required to deduct TDS under s.51 (which persons are covered)?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: Specified persons notified under s.51 — e.g., Government departments, local authorities, government agencies and other notified entities must deduct TDS.

TDS and TCS under GST.front: On what value is GST TDS/TCS computed — tax‑inclusive or tax‑exclusive?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: On taxable value (exclusive of GST): TDS 2% on taxable value (s.51); TCS 0.5% on net taxable value collected by the operator (s.52).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: By when must the deductor/operator deposit GST TDS/TCS to the government (time period and sections)?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: 10 days from the end of the month in which tax was deducted/collected (s.51(3) / s.52(3)).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: Which GST returns must be filed for TDS and TCS, and what is the due date?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: GSTR‑7 (TDS) and GSTR‑8 (TCS) — furnished by the 10th day of the month following the month of deduction/collection (s.51(2) / s.52(2)).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: Where does the deductee/supplier get the credit of GST TDS or TCS?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: In the electronic CASH ledger, after the deductor/operator files GSTR-7 / GSTR-8. It is cash, not input tax credit.

TDS and TCS under GST.front: Does TCS under s.52 apply to supplies made by the e‑commerce operator itself?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: No — s.52 applies only to taxable supplies made through the operator by other suppliers; not to supplies made by the operator as principal.

TDS and TCS under GST.front: Is there any monetary threshold below which e‑commerce TCS doesn't apply?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: No threshold for TCS—applies on all taxable supplies through the operator. TDS alone has a threshold: ₹2.5 lakh (s.51).

TDS and TCS under GST.front: What is the rate of interest for late deposit of GST TDS/TCS?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: 18% p.a. (statutory interest for delayed payment of tax) applies to late deposit of TDS/TCS under the GST interest provisions.

TDS and TCS under GST.front: When is GST TDS NOT deducted even above ₹2.5 lakh?
TDS and TCS under GST.back: When the location of the supplier AND the place of supply are both in a State different from the State of registration of the deductor (proviso to s.51(1)).

Payment of Tax.front: Order of utilising input tax credit (s.49(5), 49A)?
Payment of Tax.back: IGST credit FIRST: against IGST, then CGST and SGST in any order — and it must be exhausted before CGST/SGST credit is used. CGST credit: CGST, then IGST. SGST credit: SGST, then IGST. CGST and SGST never cross.

Payment of Tax.front: What can the electronic credit ledger NOT pay?
Payment of Tax.back: Tax under reverse charge, interest, penalty, late fee and any other amount — all must be paid in cash. The credit ledger pays OUTPUT TAX only.

Payment of Tax.front: What is the statutory rate of interest for delayed GST payment and from when is it charged?
Payment of Tax.back: 18% p.a. (s.50 CGST Act); charged from the day after the due date until the date of actual payment.

Payment of Tax.front: Can Input Tax Credit be used to pay interest, penalty, fee or other non‑tax amounts under GST?
Payment of Tax.back: No. ITC cannot be used for interest, penalty, fee or other non‑tax amounts; these must be paid from the electronic cash ledger. (s.49(2) CGST Act)
(1) Self-assessed tax and dues of PREVIOUS periods; (2) self-assessed tax and dues of the CURRENT period; (3) any other amount, including demands u/s 73/74.

Payment of Tax.front: Over-the-counter payment limit and challan validity?
Payment of Tax.back: OTC (cash, cheque, DD): up to ₹10,000 per challan per tax period. Challan GST PMT-06 is valid for 15 days.
18% p.a. — but only where the credit is wrongly availed AND utilised. Availed but lying unused in the credit ledger: no interest.

Payment of Tax.front: Interest for late payment (s.50(1)) — on what amount?
Payment of Tax.back: 18% p.a. on the portion paid through the electronic CASH ledger (net cash liability), where the return is filed late but before proceedings begin.

Returns.front: Which section mandates who must furnish GST returns and what must be furnished in brief?
Returns.back: Every registered person must furnish returns as prescribed, containing outward supplies, inward supplies/ITC and tax liability details (s.39). Returns/format/timelines are as prescribed by rules/forms.

Returns.front: By what date must the annual GST return for a financial year be filed?
Returns.back: 31 December following the end of the financial year — annual return as prescribed (s.44).

Returns.front: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B — monthly due dates?
Returns.back: GSTR-1: 11th of the following month. GSTR-3B: 20th of the following month. GSTR-3B cannot be filed until GSTR-1 for the period is filed.

Returns.front: QRMP scheme — who, and when is tax paid?
Returns.back: Aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore. Returns quarterly (GSTR-1 by 13th, GSTR-3B by 22nd/24th of the month after the quarter); tax paid MONTHLY by the 25th. Optional IFF for B2B invoices by the 13th.
CMP-08 quarterly by the 18th of the month after the quarter. GSTR-4 annually by 30 JUNE following the financial year (was 30 April).

Returns.front: What is the time limit to file a refund claim under GST?
Returns.back: 2 years from the relevant date specified in the Act — refund application time‑limit (s.54).
GSTR-9 by 31 December following the FY. GSTR-9C (self-certified) also, where aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore.

Returns.front: Late fee for GSTR-3B/GSTR-1, and the outer time limit to file?
Returns.back: ₹50 a day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST); ₹20 a day for a nil return. No return can be filed after 3 years from its due date.

Returns.front: What key condition must be satisfied for a recipient to legally avail Input Tax Credit regarding supplier returns/payments?
Returns.back: ITC is available only if recipient holds valid tax invoice, tax is charged by supplier and supplier has furnished requisite return/payments as per section 16 conditions (s.16).
